newsitem.title: JAPAN: DKB says hasn't decided on president's resignation.
newsitem.headline: DKB says hasn't decided on president's resignation.

text.p: Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank Ltd (DKB) on Thursday denied media reports that the bank had decided to seek the resignations of its chairman and president.
"The reported resignations have not been decided," a DKB spokesman said.
The Asahi Shimbun said on Thursday that DKB had decided to seek the resignation of its chairman Tadashi Okuda.
It said the bank's president Katsuhiko Kondo and its advisers would also resign to take responsibility for DKB's role in a payoff and racketeering scandal involving Nomura Securities Co Ltd.
The Asahi Shimbun said a formal decision on personnel changes would be made at a board meeting scheduled to be held on Friday.

But it added that the meeting might be postponed as DKB might want to see how prosecutors' investigation of the payoff scandal is progressing. Earlier this week, prosecutors raided DKB's headquarters and the homes of its current and former executives.
If the meeting is postponed, the bank will not be able to announce its earnings on Friday as scheduled, industry analysts said.
"We have not heard about a change in schedule for the board meeting and the earnings announcement," the DKB spokesman said.
